notes: Mutable ATO and Treasury facts behind the Payday Super timing control. Re-verify at use time. This index is provenance, not a substitute for a live source check.

sources.title: ATO Payday Super
sources.fact: For paydays from 1 July 2026, the ordinary period requires the fund to receive the contribution, with enough information to allocate it, by the end of the seventh business day after the payday.

sources.title: ATO Payday Super for employers
sources.fact: Allowable longer periods (first eligible contribution, qualifying out-of-cycle payments, exceptional circumstances, s 18C alignment) are fact-dependent. A remittance date is not fund receipt.

sources.title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Payday Superannuation) Act 2025, Schedule 1 / SGAA s 18C
sources.fact: Statutory payday-super timing and the s 18C alignment conditions sit in this Act. Missing facts produce UNKNOWN, not a forecast legally mandatory date.

sources.title: Superannuation Guarantee (Administration) Regulations 2018
sources.fact: Use the current compilation, including the 1 July 2026 compilation where that is the law in force for the weeks being forecast.

sources.title: ATO: Denying deductions for ATO interest charges
sources.fact: Read 26 September 2026 (page last updated 8 June 2026). GIC and SIC incurred on or after 1 July 2025 are not deductible for income years starting on or after that date, whatever year the debt relates to, and a later remission of such an amount is not assessable. GIC or SIC incurred before 1 July 2025 remains deductible for 2024-25 and earlier years, and a later remission of a deducted amount is assessable. An entity with a substituted accounting period loses the deduction from its next accounting period starting after 1 July 2025. GIC on unpaid income tax is incurred daily; SIC is incurred in the year the amended assessment notice is served.
sources.limitations: ATO summary of the law change. Confirm the provisions of the Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Incentives and Integrity) Act 2025 for the period at use time.
